title: librosa beat tracking
text: Tempo estimates describe beat rate in beats per minute. Onset strength and beat tracking estimate periodic activity; half-time and double-time ambiguities can occur. Tempo alone does not determine rhythmic similarity.

title: librosa chroma features
text: Chroma summarizes energy across twelve pitch classes. It is a harmonic and pitch-pattern proxy, not a transcription of melody or proof that tunes are identical.

title: librosa dynamic time warping
text: Dynamic time warping aligns ordered feature sequences with different timing. Chroma alignment can compare harmonic progressions while allowing time stretching. It does not identify copying.

title: librosa spectral centroid
text: The spectral centroid is the weighted mean frequency of a spectrum. Spectral statistics and MFCCs summarize sound color or timbre but cannot establish an instrument identity.

title: MERT research paper
text: MERT is a pretrained music representation encoder. Frozen embeddings can support downstream tasks, but cosine similarity is not a calibrated probability of musical similarity or an instrument prediction.

title: Official FMA dataset repository
text: FMA supplies music audio, metadata, genres, and train validation test splits. Genre classification evaluates representation quality; matching genre labels does not establish human similarity judgments.

title: AST AudioSet model and official preprocessing
text: Audio Spectrogram Transformer predicts AudioSet sound-event classes from log-Mel features at 16 kHz. Musical-instrument class scores are model outputs, not verified identities, calibrated similarity probabilities or absence proofs. Predictions only describe analyzed excerpts; reliability on these recordings requires instrument annotations.

title: EnCodec: High Fidelity Neural Audio Compression
text: EnCodec encodes waveforms into residual vector-quantized audio codes for reconstruction. Token distributions can be compared as exploratory texture descriptors. Tokens do not directly identify instruments, production techniques or vocal delivery; human similarity requires separate validation.
